config.title: React Server Components & SSR vs SSG

intro.title: React Server Components & SSR vs SSG
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that demonstrates server-side rendering (SSR) concepts, similar to the principles behind React Server Components and static site generation (SSG). You'll learn how to create components that can be pre-rendered on the server for faster initial page loads and better SEO. The core programming concept involves using Angular's built-in tools for SSR and understanding the differences between server-side and client-side rendering. You'll work with Angular components, TypeScript, and the Angular CLI to set up and configure rendering modes, focusing on when to use SSR versus SSG for optimal performance.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for building high-performance, SEO-friendly web applications like e-commerce product pages, news websites, and content-heavy dashboards. For example, a product listing page uses SSR to render initial product cards and prices quickly for search engines, while interactive filters and 'Add to Cart' buttons are handled client-side. Similarly, a news article page might use SSG to pre-render static content for fast loading, with dynamic elements like live comment sections or personalized recommendations loaded separately. Understanding when to use server-side rendering, static generation, or client components helps developers optimize performance and user experience in real-world applications.

objectives: Construct an Angular component that renders static content at build time using server-side generation
Configure an Angular application to enable server-side rendering for dynamic content delivery
Implement data fetching within server-side rendered components to populate templates
Manipulate component rendering strategies by switching between SSR and SSG configurations
Integrate client-side hydration with server-rendered components for interactive functionality
Apply appropriate rendering techniques based on content type and performance requirements
Initialize Angular Universal in a project to enable server-side capabilities

steps.title: Import Angular core modules and components
steps.instruction: Import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbols you need from their respective Angular packages.

// Import CommonModule from '@angular/common'

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Add component metadata with template and styles
steps.instruction: Add the selector, templateUrl, and styleUrls properties to the @Component decorator of your AppComponent. Use 'app-root' for selector, './app.component.html' for templateUrl, and ['./app.component.css'] for styleUrls.
steps.hint: The @Component decorator should include these three properties. Make sure styleUrls is an array with the CSS file path.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will have its metadata configured for rendering with a template and styles.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes selector: 'app-root', templateUrl: './app.component.html', and styleUrls: ['./app.component.css'].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some metadata, but check that all three properties (selector, templateUrl, styleUrls) are present with the correct values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component metadata is missing or incorrect. Make sure to add selector, templateUrl, and styleUrls properties to the @Component decorator.

steps.title: Initialize component state with server-side rendering flag
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, create a property called isServerRendered and set its initial value to true.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration with type annotation in the class body, like 'propertyName: type = initialValue'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state property that tracks whether it was rendered on the server, which is important for understanding SSR concepts.
successCriteria: The AppComponent class contains a property named isServerRendered with type boolean and initial value true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the property is named exactly 'isServerRendered' with type boolean and initial value true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The property wasn't added correctly. Remember to create a property called 'isServerRendered' with type boolean and set it to true inside the AppComponent class.

steps.title: Add ngOnInit lifecycle hook
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, add the ngOnInit() method to demonstrate component initialization for server-side rendering awareness.
steps.hint: Implement the ngOnInit method from the OnInit interface you already imported.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class now has a properly implemented ngOnInit lifecycle method.
successCriteria: The ngOnInit method is defined with a void return type and empty body in the AppComponent class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the ngOnInit method with the correct syntax and placed it inside the AppComponent class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnInit method is missing or has incorrect syntax. Remember to implement it as part of the AppComponent class that implements the OnInit interface.

successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes a template property with a header element containing a title about server-side rendering.

steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a paragraph element that displays the current value of the isServerRendered property using Angular interpolation syntax.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind the property value inside the paragraph text.

Server-side rendering enabled: {{ isServerRendered }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show a paragraph that dynamically displays whether server-side rendering is enabled based on the component's state.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the template that uses interpolation to display the isServerRendered property value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
